title: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome in alcoholic hepatitis: Hepatic encephalopathy a common theme
case_prompt:
A 40-year-old woman with a history of severe alcoholic hepatitis complicated by grade 3 hepatic encephalopathy was readmitted less than 24 hours after discharge following a witnessed tonic–clonic seizure. She had no prior history of seizures and reported strict abstinence from alcohol and nonprescription drugs since her last hospitalization, with documented compliance with lactulose and rifaximin. 

On arrival, her temperature was 97.2°F, pulse 95/min, respiratory rate 8/min, and blood pressure 114/78 mmHg. Off sedation, she had no focal neurologic deficits. Laboratory studies showed hemoglobin 10.0 g/dL, INR 1.79, creatinine 0.3 mg/dL, total bilirubin 10.8 mg/dL, ALT 54 IU/L, AST 112 IU/L, bicarbonate 15.5 mmol/L, anion gap 21 mEq/L, unchanged from prior discharge. Urine toxicology was negative, and blood alcohol level was undetectable.

A brain MRI performed while the patient remained postictal showed high signal intensity in the subcortical and periventricular white matter of the bilateral temporal and parietal lobes on FLAIR images, similar in distribution to a limited prior study. A 60-minute EEG revealed high focal epileptogenic potential in the same temporal-parietal regions.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Alcohol withdrawal considered — “She did not consume alcohol or non-prescription drugs between discharge and readmission.”  
2. Hepatic encephalopathy considered — “Despite appropriate therapy with lactulose and rifaximin, the patient remained grade 3 hepatic encephalopathy.”  
3. Drug abuse considered — “Urine drug screen was negative and alcohol level was undetectable.”  
4. Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome confirmed — “A repeat MRI … showed a high signal intensity in the subcortical … white matter of the bilateral temporal and parietal lobes on the fluid attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequence of MRI … consistent with PRES.”
